bull_case: The approved heart/liver/lung platform doubles again over five years while Kidney, Gen 3 and Europe extend the runway beyond a decade and NOP captures more value per transplant.
bear_case: Core U.S. liver/heart adoption matures within five years, Kidney is delayed, international reimbursement remains limited and logistics complexity absorbs much of the economic growth.
thesis: A five-year doubling is plausible without heroic assumptions: 2026 revenue guidance is about $747M at midpoint, the U.S. platform is still growing, and Kidney/Gen 3/international logistics create additional vectors. The 5-10 year duration is credible, but the current price already approximates the locked Base DCF, so the market-misperception element is only moderate rather than a clear outlier expectation gap.

evidence.claim: 2026 revenue guidance is $737M-$757M, representing 22%-25% growth and excluding PAD Aviation revenue and incremental ENHANCE Part B/DENOVO trial revenue.
Management is investing in OCS Kidney and Gen 3 while beginning a European organ-logistics network through PAD Aviation.
Revenue expanded from $241.6M in 2023 to $605.5M in 2025, demonstrating the ability to scale the platform before the new growth vectors contribute materially.
Locked Base valuation from the triage run is close to the $86.42 cutoff price, limiting evidence that the market is underestimating a clearly identified long-term fact.

counterevidence: U.S. liver already dominates revenue, so doubling from the current base requires broader organ, volume or geographic expansion.
International reimbursement is not established at U.S. scale.
Kidney and Gen 3 are development programs, not current approved commercial revenue streams.
Founder-led execution is strong but the material weakness and increasing operational complexity temper culture confidence.
unknowns: Kidney commercial launch date and addressable economics.
Five-year transplant volume penetration by heart/liver/lung.
Whether market expectations already capitalize most of the new-product optionality.
falsifiers: If 2027-2028 growth falls to low single digits before Kidney/international contribution, the five-year opportunity score should be cut.
A successful Kidney launch with strong unit economics would extend duration and opportunity scale.
A meaningful price discount to unchanged Base economics could raise the market-misperception score.

subscores.rationale: A >2x five-year path is plausible from continued U.S. OCS/NOP penetration plus new-organ and international vectors without requiring a single heroic market-share assumption.
The approved platform plus Kidney, Gen 3 and geography support a 5-10 year runway, but >10-year durability is not yet proven.
The founder-led organization successfully added NOP/logistics to the original device model, but internal-control and scaling complexity prevent a 75+ score.
The long-term opportunity is real, but cutoff price is near locked Base value, so evidence of a concrete market underestimation is limited.

uncertainties.rationale: The doubling path depends partly on unapproved or early international initiatives.
Ten-year durability depends on repeated product renewal and transplant-policy stability.
The organization is scaling across devices, aviation and international operations simultaneously.
Reverse DCF shows little obvious margin of safety; market expectations are not directly observable beyond price.
